sections.heading: Is Fusion Markets Worth Your Money in 2026?
sections.body:
Four dollars and fifty cents per standard lot round-turn. That is the number that defines Fusion Markets. While Tickmill charges $6, IC Markets charges $7, and Pepperstone charges $7 — Fusion charges $4.50. Thirty-six percent cheaper than the industry average, verified by their own public data. For a trader executing 200 lots per month, that saving is $300-500 monthly compared to a $7 RT broker. Over a year, $3,600-6,000. Enough to matter.

ASIC regulated since 2017 from Melbourne. Zero minimum deposit. Raw spreads from 0.0 pips. TradingView integration via cTrader. MT4 and MT5 also available. The Trustpilot rating sits at 4.8/5 from 4,800+ reviews with 86% five-star — traders who use Fusion Markets tend to stay and recommend it.

The catch is scope. Two hundred and fifty instruments is genuinely limited. No FCA or CySEC licence means UK and EU clients trade through offshore VFSC or FSA entities without compensation schemes. Education and research are non-existent — this is not a broker that teaches you to trade. It is a broker that executes your trades at the lowest possible cost. Know the difference before you sign up.

sections.heading: Is Fusion Markets Regulated? — Licence Check 2026
sections.body:
Single Tier-1 licence. Fusion Markets Pty Ltd holds ASIC licence 385620 — confirmed active. The VFSC (Vanuatu) and FSA (Seychelles) entities serve international clients with higher leverage but no compensation scheme.

The critical distinction: only Australian residents trade under ASIC protection. UK residents accepted but routed through VFSC — no FSCS coverage. EU residents similarly through offshore entities — no ICF protection. If you are outside Australia, your regulatory protection is limited to fund segregation and Fusion's operational integrity.

No enforcement actions from ASIC or any regulator documented. No presence on FCA, ASIC, or CySEC warning lists. Eight years of operation without incident. Fund segregation across all entities. NAFT last reviewed Fusion Markets regulation in May 2026.

sections.heading: Fusion Markets Spreads, Fees and Accounts — What Do You Actually Pay in 2026?
sections.body:
Two accounts. Zero: 0.0 pips raw spread plus $2.25 per side ($4.50 round-turn). Classic: spread-only with markup built in, approximately 0.8 pips EUR/USD average — all-in around $8 per lot. The Zero account is the entire point of this broker.

At $4.50 RT, Fusion Markets is $1.50 cheaper per lot than Tickmill ($6), $1.50 cheaper than FP Markets ($6), and $2.50 cheaper than IC Markets or Pepperstone ($7). This is not a marginal difference — it is a structural cost advantage that compounds with volume. Twenty trades per day, five days per week, fifty weeks per year: that $2.50 saving versus Pepperstone is $12,500 annually.

The cTrader commission structure differs slightly: $2.25 per $100,000 of notional volume for forex, $1.20 per $100,000 for metals. Zero commission on US share CFDs, crypto, and oil.

No inactivity fee. No deposit fees. No withdrawal fees. The cleanest, cheapest cost structure in regulated forex.

The positive pattern: smooth, fast, fee-free processing. Traders praise the simplicity — no games, no friction, no unexpected delays. The no-frills philosophy extends to withdrawals: request, process, receive. The low complaint ratio relative to review volume is the strongest signal.
